title: Generative AI may backfire for counterspeech
findings: The paper's general findings apply to all categories of hate speech studied, including religious hate speech. It found that non-contextualized counterspeech using a warning-of-consequence strategy significantly reduced the number of hateful posts. However, contextualized counterspeech generated by LLMs proved ineffective and could even backfire, for instance by increasing online hostility or toxicity, regardless of the counterspeech strategy (empathy or warning).

measurement_description: Effectiveness of AI-generated counterspeech in reducing online religious hate speech. The study sampled hateful posts using keywords related to religious groups (e.g., jew, muslim, islam, jihad) and measured whether counterspeech replies led to users deleting hateful posts, posting fewer hateful posts, or changing the toxicity of their language.
